chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: He said Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

regarding the Qunut: 'If you wish, perform Qunut, and if you wish, do not perform Qunut.' Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'And when there is Taqiyya (prudent dissimulation), do not perform Qunut, and I take this upon myself.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan (Imam al-Rida, peace be upon him)
key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir, peace be upon him)
key_terms.التَّقِيَّةُ: Taqiyya (prudent dissimulation or concealment of faith)

ai.seo_question: Is Qunut in prayer obligatory or optional according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the juristic status of Qunut as a recommended (mustahabb) act rather than an obligatory one, granting worshippers flexibility. It introduces a specific practical dimension where Qunut is omitted during periods of Taqiyya, reflecting the Imam’s personal adherence to this precautionary measure to avoid political or social risk. This highlights the dynamic nature of Shia fiqh, where ritual acts can be modified based on contextual circumstances of safety and authority.
